Connect to an OmicIDX release

Source: R/connect.R
omicidx_connect.Rd

Opens an in-memory DuckDB database and makes an OmicIDX release available in it. Nothing is downloaded up front: queries read the remote Parquet files over HTTPS, fetching only the columns and row groups they need.

Usage

omicidx_connect(version = "latest")

Arguments

version

character(1). "latest" (default), a date "YYYY-MM-DD" or a month "YYYY-MM". See the Versions section.

Value

A DuckDB DBI::DBIConnection. Close it with DBI::dbDisconnect(). omicidx_release() tells which release it is connected to.

Details

After connecting, tables are referenced as schema.table, for example sradb.study or geometadb.gsm. Use omicidx_tables() to list them and omicidx_db() for tab-completable dplyr tables.

Versions

  • "latest": the nightly build at https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/.

  • "YYYY-MM-DD": a dated nightly build, kept for 30 days.

  • "YYYY-MM": a monthly release on HuggingFace (omicidx/omicidx@YYYY-MM). Monthly releases are kept long term and are the version to cite. Connecting takes longer (about 30 seconds) because DuckDB inspects every Parquet file while it creates the views. HuggingFace limits anonymous requests (3000 per 5 minutes per IP address) and one query can make hundreds, so heavy use can fail with HTTP 429 until the window resets.

Requests carry the User-Agent omicidxr/<package version>. DuckDB extensions (httpfs, json) are downloaded once and cached in tools::R_user_dir("omicidxr", "cache"). The connection neither uses ~/.duckdb nor reads DuckDB secrets persisted there.

Examples

con <- omicidx_connect()
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT count(*) AS n FROM sradb.study")
#>        n
#> 1 775033
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
